{{nihongo|'''Oomahiko Shrine'''|大麻比古神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

{{wikidata link|Q11442033|ja|大麻比古神社 (徳島市)|grok=none|check_date=2026-06-06}}

=== History ===
It is said that Kōno Yakichirō, son of a retainer who moved from Kōno-no-shō in {{ill|Iyo Province|Q907829|qid=Q907829}} to {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|Q907457|qid=Q907457}} and served the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|Q2975261|qid=Q2975261}}, welcomed the {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}} of Ōmahiko Shrine from Ichinomiya in {{ill|Myōdō District, Tokushima|Q1156486|qid=Q1156486}} in {{ill|1653|ab|1653|af|1653|als|1653|am|1653 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1653|ar|1653|ary|1653|arz|1653|ast|1653|avk|1653|az|1653|azb|۱۶۵۳ (میلادی)|ban|1653|bcl|1653|be|1653|be_x_old|1653|bg|1653|bn|১৬৫৩|bpy|মারি ১৬৫৩|br|1653|bs|1653.|ca|1653|cdo|1653 nièng|ce|1653 шо|ceb|1653|ckb|١٦٥٣|crh|1653|cs|1653|cv|1653|cy|1653|da|1653|de|1653|diq|1653|el|1653|eml|1653|eo|1653|es|1653|et|1653|eu|1653|fa|۱۶۵۳ (میلادی)|fi|1653|fo|1653|fr|1653|frp|1653|frr|1653|fur|1653|fy|1653|ga|1653|gan|1653年|gcr|1653|gd|1653|gl|1653|gv|1653|he|1653|hi|१६५३|hr|1653.|ht|1653 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1653|hy|1653|hyw|1653 թուական|ia|1653|id|1653|ilo|1653|io|1653|is|1653|it|1653|ja|1653年|jv|1653|ka|1653|kaa|1653|kk|1653 жыл|kn|೧೬೫೩|ko|1653년|krc|1653 джыл|la|1653|lb|1653|li|1653|lij|1653|lmo|1653|lt|1653 m.|lv|1653. gads|mai|१६५३|map_bms|1653|mdf|1653|mg|1653|mhr|1653|mi|1653|mk|1653|mr|इ.स. १६५३|mrj|1653 и|ms|1653|my|၁၆၅၃|mzn|۱۶۵۳|nah|1653|nap|1653|nds|1653|new|सन् १६५३|nl|1653|nn|1653|no|1653|nrm|1653|nso|1653|oc|1653|olo|1653|or|୧୬୫୩|os|1653-æм аз|pl|1653|pnb|1653|pt|1653|qu|1653|ro|1653|ru|1653 год|rue|1653|sa|१६५३|sah|1653|scn|1653|sd|1653ع|se|1653|sh|1653.|shn|1653|simple|1653|sk|1653|sl|1653|smn|1653|sq|1653|sr|1653|su|1653|sv|1653|sw|1653|szl|1653|ta|1653|tg|Соли 1653|th|พ.ศ. 2196|tk|1653|tl|1653|tr|1653|tt|1653 ел|uk|1653|ur|1653ء|uz|1653|vec|1653|vi|1653|vls|1653|vo|1653|wa|1653|war|1653|wuu|1653年|xmf|1653|yi|1653|zea|1653|zh|1653年|zh_min_nan|1653 nî|zh_yue|1653年|qid=Q6965}} ({{ill|Jōō (Edo period)|Q1145081|qid=Q1145081}} 2), making it the guardian shrine of the Kōno family. There is also a theory identifying it with the {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} "Manotohiko Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}. It was originally called Yakichi Myōjin, but in {{ill|1870|Q7741|qid=Q7741}} (Meiji 3) the name was changed to the current one, and it was listed as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.
